label: Dexterity_Heffner1975 (score)
measures_what: Ordinal digital-dexterity rank 1-7 for 69 mammals, assigned mostly from hand anatomy via the Fig.1 algorithm (1=fused/restrained digits; 2=separate non-convergent; 3=convergent non-prehensile; 4=prehensile, non-opposable thumb; 5=pseudo-opposable thumb; 6=opposable thumb/power grip; 7=opposable thumb/precision grip)
primary_sources_cited: The study itself (authors' own scale); scale is an extension of Napier 1961 and Napier & Napier 1967 (Napier 1960 cited for 'precision grip') - the accompanying pyramidal-tract anatomy is compiled from cited literature, but the dexterity rank is Heffner & Masterton's own
basis: Originator of the canonical scale: canonical label is defined in variable_definitions_live.csv as 'digital dexterity score (Heffner & Masterton scale)' with definition_source Iwaniuk_etal_1999 Table1 definitions, whose note says 'same trait as Heffner & Masterton 1975/1983 digital dexterity'. Its 1-7 anchors match 1983 Table II rank-for-rank and its values are identical to 1983 for all 21 shared species and to Iwaniuk for all 25 Iwaniuk species (by binomial/common name), so the repo note 'the three dexterity scales differ' is not supported for 1975
evidence: Heffner & Masterton 1975 PDF (repo Heffner_Masterton_1975/Heffner-1975-Variation in form of the pyramid1.pdf, fetched via GitHub raw) 'Scale for Digital Dexterity' pp.176-177: 'no commonly used index of digital dexterity that is applicable to all mammals. Therefore, we were forced to derive a suitable scale of our own (fig. 1). The dexterity scale in figure 1 is an extension of one invented by NAPIER [1961] and NAPIER and NAPIER [1967]. The scale ranks animals from 1 to 7 mostly on the basis of the anatomy of their hand... rank of 1... fusion of its phalanges... rank of 7... truly opposable thumb and capable of a precision grip'; Fig.1 p.177 algorithm anchors 1 fused/restrained to 7 precision grip; repo Heffner_Masterton_1975_TableI_definitions.csv: 'digital dexterity rank (1-7); higher = greater dexterity' (69 rows)

label: Dexterity_Heffner1983 (score)
measures_what: Ordinal digital-dexterity rank 1-7 for 21 grade-selected species (17 primates plus hedgehogs x2, opossum and tree shrew), using the same hand-anatomy anchors as 1975, presented verbally in Table II (1=fused/restrained digits to 7=opposable thumb capable of precision grip in opposition to each finger)
primary_sources_cited: Heffner & Masterton 1975 for the method/values (1983 states the method was 'described previously'); scale derived from Bishop 1964, Napier 1960, Napier 1961 and Napier & Napier 1967 (Table II footnote)
basis: Not a revised or distinct scale: 1983 explicitly reuses the 1975 method, Table II anchors match the 1975 Fig.1 algorithm rank-for-rank (only rank 6 is worded more fully as 'power grip and limited precision'), and all 21 species in 1983 Table I have dexterity values identical to their 1975 Table I values (verified from repo Table I CSVs, 21/21, no mismatches). It is a smaller phyletic-grade subset/re-presentation of the 1975 variable, so it groups into the canonical H&M scale
evidence: Heffner & Masterton 1983 PDF (repo Heffner_Masterton_1983/Heffner-1983-The role of the corticospinal tra.pdf, fetched via GitHub raw) 'Derivation of Numerical Parameters - Digital Dexterity Scale' pp.167-168: 'A method for ranking digital dexterity in a wide range of mammals has been described previously [Heffner and Masterton, 1975]. It is based primarily on Napier's analysis of hand anatomy and the hand's normal use [Napier and Napier, 1967]. A rank (from 1 to 7) has been assigned... The meanings of the ranks are given in table II'; Table II p.170 lists ranks 1-7 with the anchors quoted in measures_what and footnote 'Scale derived from Bishop [1964], Napier [1960, 1961], and Napier and Napier [1967]' (also repo Heffner_Masterton_1983_Tables.xlsx sheet 'Table II - Dexterity Scale'); repo 1983 definitions: 'digital dexterity rank (1-7); scale defined in Table II'

label: Dexterity_Iwaniuk1999 (score)
measures_what: Ordinal digital-dexterity index 1-7 for 25 mammalian species (12-13 primates plus other mammals), taken unchanged from Heffner & Masterton - i.e. the same hand-anatomy/Napier-based rank (observed values 1 goat/armadillo to 7 human), not a new behavioural scoring
primary_sources_cited: Heffner & Masterton 1975 [ref 32] and Heffner & Masterton 1983 [ref 31] - dexterity 'was taken from Heffner and Masterton'; the index itself is based on Napier 1961 [ref 47] per Discussion 4.3
basis: Compilation/re-analysis carrier under the owner's rule, not an independent scale: Iwaniuk et al. is a re-analysis of the H&M data set, selected only the 25 species with both tract length and depth known, and reprinted H&M dexterity values unchanged (verified: all 25 match 1975 Table I by binomial or common name, incl. rat 3 and chimpanzee 6, even though Discussion 4.3 argues those should be 5-6 and 7 - they criticise the index but do not re-score it). Canonical 'Dexterity (1-7 scale)' is itself sourced from Iwaniuk Table 1 definitions, so this suffixed label duplicates the canonical exactly
evidence: Iwaniuk et al. 1999 text (repo PDF text) Abstract/title: 'a re-analysis of the Heffner and Masterton data set'; Methods 2.1 Data p.175: 'Data on the length and depth of the corticospinal tracts and dexterity of 25 species were taken from reports cited in Heffner and Masterton [31,32] (Table 1). Only 25 out of the original 69 species were examined...'; Table 1 footnote p.175: 'The dexterity index, a measurement of the digit dexterity of a species, was taken from Heffner and Masterton [31,32]'; Discussion 4.3 pp.181-182: 'the presently used dexterity index (based upon Napier [47]) has some serious flaws'; repo Iwaniuk_etal_1999_Table1_definitions.csv Dexterity: 'digital dexterity score (Heffner & Masterton scale)... same trait as Heffner & Masterton 1975/1983 digital dexterity' and Iwaniuk Table1.ReadMe.md: 'the Dexterity column is the same digital-dexterity score'
